title: PKU apps & software
source_note: Compiled from App Store / Google Play listings, developer and manufacturer sites (Cycle Pharmaceuticals, Nutricia/Danone, Vitaflo/Nestle Health Science, Ajinomoto Cambrooke), the flok / National PKU News nonprofit, howmuchphe.org, community app roundups, and the Cureledger / PKU Commons project pages for Phebe. Market-facing facts only: who builds each tool, business model, platform, and whether it survives. The recurring pattern across the category is fragmentation into many solo- or small-shop apps that go unmaintained when one developer moves on; PKU Commons exists as a response to exactly that survival problem. Cost, backing, and status are marked estimate where a listing did not state them explicitly.

records.name: Phebe
records.notes: Early-stage AI phe-estimator that reads a nutrition label 'the way a PKU parent would', estimates phe, and logs it; positioned as the reference implementation of the open PKU Commons accuracy standard rather than a finished market leader. Honest about thin data and AI-assisted estimation. Its survival strategy is the point: built on shared open infrastructure so the tool outlives any single developer, the failure mode that kills most PKU apps.
records.market_signal: Only entrant pairing an AI estimator with a public, reproducible accuracy benchmark and open infrastructure; the differentiator is verifiable reliability and continuity, not features.

sources.title: PKU Commons - families page (download & test Phebe)

records.name: flok (formerly PKU News)
records.notes: Free app and research platform for inherited metabolic disorders (PKU, HCU, MSUD, organic acidemias, tyrosinemia, urea cycle disorders); rebrand of the long-running National PKU News nonprofit. Food database of 10,000+ items with six amino acids, plus mood/symptom/lab tracking, wearable integration (Apple Health / Google Fit), and patient-led research. Nonprofit backing is the strongest survival signal in the category.
records.market_signal: The nonprofit consolidator: multi-IMD scope plus a research arm gives it durability that solo apps lack; competes on trust and longevity rather than a single feature.

sources.title: flok Health on the App Store

records.name: How Much Phe (HowMuchPhe.org)
records.developer: National PKU News (now flok); built by Sarah Chamberlin
records.notes: The classic web-based phe-counting database, launched July 2014 from the Low Protein Food List for PKU; phe/protein/exchange/calorie values for 10,000+ foods with intake and blood-level charting and export. Reported 2,500+ subscribers and 1,000+ daily users. Now being folded into the flok platform, showing consolidation of the nonprofit tooling.
records.market_signal: Deepest curated food database in the space and a scholarship/clinic model for access; its migration into flok signals the category consolidating around one nonprofit spine.

records.name: Cycle Vita PKU
records.notes: AI-powered PKU management app launched April 2025 by a pharma company; searchable 9,000+ food database, an AI meal scanner that estimates phe from a photo, plus lab-result tracking and medication/formula reminders. Pharma backing means real budget and likely durability, but the app steers toward the maker's treatment ecosystem. Targeted at adolescents/young adults gaining independence.
records.market_signal: First well-funded AI-photo phe estimator; pharma money solves the maintenance problem but raises the question of neutrality vs. an independent, verifiable standard.

records.name: EasyPKU
records.notes: Tracks phe, protein, exchanges, formula, and calories; GDPR-compliant with encrypted cloud storage, multi-user family sharing, blood-level graphs, and export. Partnered with the Norwegian PKU Association since 2022 (members act as test users). Three subscription tiers give it a real revenue model, which is unusual and a survival positive in a category dominated by free solo apps.
records.market_signal: Rare working subscription business model plus a national patient-org partnership; proves families will pay for family-sharing and reliability.

sources.title: EasyPKU - The Leading PKU App Worldwide

records.name: PKU Tools
records.notes: All-in-one tool (scale, nutrition table, calculator) with food-database search, barcode scanning, and a phe/protein converter; also lets the user describe or photograph a food and have AI estimate weight and nutrition. Solo-developed lineage dating to 2013; last updated April 2025, so currently maintained but carries classic single-developer continuity risk.
records.market_signal: Shows solo devs are already bolting AI photo-estimation onto legacy apps; feature-competitive but one person away from going stale.

sources.title: PKU Tools: All-in-One Nutrition App for PKU

records.name: PKU Diet - Phenylketonuria
records.notes: For families and children on phe-restricted diets; calculates phe, protein, calories, fat, carbs and protein equivalent, supports custom products, and tracks amino acids per product/meal/day. A widely-listed solo-built app; classic single-developer maintenance exposure.
records.market_signal: Broad reach on both stores off a solo build; illustrates how thin the wall is between 'popular' and 'abandoned' when there is one maintainer.

sources.title: PKU Diet on the App Store

records.name: DietAssistant for PKU
records.notes: Daily food logging with a branded-food database, supermarket barcode scanning, phe-or-protein tracking, and blood-value charting; built by a developer who has PKU. Patient-built apps carry strong domain credibility but the same lone-maintainer survival risk.
records.market_signal: Patient-founder credibility is a real trust asset; the gap is continuity and verified accuracy, not empathy.

sources.title: DietAssistant for PKU on the App Store

records.name: PKU Bite
records.developer: Imobisoft Ltd with 5 specialist IMD dietitians (NSPKU-aligned)
records.notes: Reference/education app covering 1,100+ specialist and regular low-protein foods, colour-coded by the NSPKU traffic-light system into exchange-free, avoid, and count-as-exchange categories. Built over two years with a dietitian team; subject of a published efficacy study, giving it more clinical validation than most.
records.market_signal: Clinician-authored content plus a peer-reviewed efficacy study is a differentiator; more a curated food guide than a live estimator, leaving the AI-estimation lane open.

Efficacy of a New Low-Protein Multimedia Diet App for PKU (Nutrients)

records.name: MyPKU
records.notes: Looks up protein and phe per 100g from trusted public nutrition databases, lets users save frequently-used items, and check labels before buying. Lightweight label-check and logging tool; team size and business model not disclosed.
records.market_signal: Signals demand for a fast in-store label checker; underspecified backing makes its longevity unclear.

records.name: Metabolic Diet App
records.notes: Free online portal with per-disorder trackers across multiple inherited metabolic disorders, including a PKU module for families and children on phe-restricted diets. Multi-disorder scope suggests an institutional rather than solo origin, but funding and maintenance owner are not clearly stated.
records.market_signal: Multi-disorder free portal competes with flok on breadth; unclear funding leaves its survival an open question.

records.name: PKU Manager / Phe Rechner
records.developer: Solo developer (creator of the early Android app 'Phe Rechner')
records.notes: PKU Manager descends from Phe Rechner, one of the first PKU apps for Android, and is associated with the PKU Tools ecosystem. Represents the early-generation solo-built German-language phe calculators; current maintenance and store availability are uncertain, an example of the aging-solo-app risk.
records.market_signal: Emblem of the first solo-app generation; several such apps are semi-abandoned, which is the exact continuity gap PKU Commons targets.

records.name: Nutricia Homeward MyConneX / LowPro App
records.notes: MyConneX manages monthly Nutricia Homeward orders of medical nutrition supplies; the separate LowPro App tracks protein/exchange intake, protein-substitute doses, and blood levels, and the Nutricia Learning Center hosts diet-record tools for clinic visits. Manufacturer-funded and durable, but oriented around ordering and using Nutricia's own products.
records.market_signal: Formula makers use companion apps to lock in the infant-to-adult product relationship; tracking is a retention tool, not a neutral estimator.

sources.title: Nutricia Homeward MyConneX on the App Store

records.name: VitafriendsPKU
records.notes: Online support resource for patients using Vitaflo PKU protein substitutes: how to make and take each product, flavors, age-specific guidance, and recipes. A brand-support and adherence portal rather than a standalone phe-tracking app; funded by Nestle Health Science.
records.market_signal: Manufacturer support content is a retention lever around its formulas; leaves independent day-to-day phe estimation to third-party apps.

records.name: Cambrooke (Ajinomoto) recipes & PKU resources
records.notes: Cambrooke, founded in 2000 by parents of two children with PKU, offers Glytactin/GMP formulas plus recipe and metabolic-formula resources, but no confirmed dedicated phe-tracking or estimator app was found, only web recipe and product resources. Included to mark the absence: a major manufacturer without a companion tracking app.
records.market_signal: A manufacturer-shaped hole: Cambrooke has the parent-founder story and product line but no app, an obvious partnership or white-label opening.

records.name: Aptatek phenyx (POC phe monitor app)
records.notes: Companion app to a portable point-of-care phenylalanine blood monitor (disposable cartridge + Bluetooth reader); the app guides the finger-prick test and shares results with clinicians. This is blood-phe self-monitoring hardware, distinct from dietary phe estimation, but a notable tech entrant in PKU self-management.
records.market_signal: Home phe blood monitoring is the adjacent frontier; pairing device-measured phe with dietary estimation would close the loop no current diet app can.

records.name: Comidamed PKU resources
records.notes: Comidamed markets comida-PKU medical foods and publishes a PKU 'Applications' resource page, but no standalone phe-tracking app was confirmed; it appears to be primarily a nutrition company with web resources. Marked low confidence pending a confirmed app.
records.market_signal: Another manufacturer with product resources but no tracking app; reinforces that the software layer is largely left to third parties.
